headline: Brent $110.6, Kospi -3.7%, Nasdaq fut -0.3%, 10y 5.11%, OAT-Bund 144bp, Oct hold 83%
stance: Oil back above $110 on Hormuz mines, Monday's AI bounce sold in Asia, CDS protection still bid. Fed sidelined to Oct 28; oil and AI credit set the 10y this week.

news.head: ABB -6% on a 17% net-income miss; orders +40%, a record
news.body: Q3 orders $12.1bn, data-center orders up triple digits; net income $1.18bn, 17% below consensus. New 51% low-voltage JV with Mitsubishi Electric in Japan.

news.head: 3M +4.4% pre-market on an Amazon data-center warrant
news.body: Amazon expanded its data-center partnership with 3M. It took a warrant for about $521m of 3M stock, vesting on purchases of data-center products.

news.head: Cleveland-Cliffs beats, guides 2027 EBITDA above $4bn
news.body: Q3 adj EPS $0.28 vs $0.22 consensus; EBITDA $612m against a $575m guide. Steel Dynamics missed, -4.6% after hours.

news.head: CoreWeave -2.9% pre-market after a 52-week low Monday
news.body: Closed lower Monday despite an upgrade to buy and ETF dip-buying; hit a 52-week low intraday. 5y CDS held at distressed levels through the equity bounce.

implications: Oil erased the waiver discount in one session: Hormuz sets the price, not Russian diesel. With October hold at 83%, $110 Brent lands on the Dec 9 FOMC.
The AI bounce is a US-hours trade: Asia sold it, CDS did not tighten, hedgers moved from puts to protection. Equity lows hold only if credit confirms.

watch.head: Housing starts and Philly Fed services, 8:30am
watch.body: Fed blackout to the Oct 28 FOMC. API crude stocks after the close; claims Thursday, Michigan final Friday.

watch.head: Netflix and SpaceX report after today's close
watch.body: Netflix consensus EPS $0.82 on $12.88bn revenue. Options price a 7.5% SpaceX move by Friday. Meta, Tesla, IBM, TI Wednesday after the close.

watch.head: Hormuz: Pakistan's army chief in Tehran today
watch.body: Qatar: talks on "increasingly difficult" ground. Iran lists 122 tankers for transit violations, 19 negotiating removal. Gulf flows near 80% of pre-war.

watch.head: France: budget revenue vote, second protest weekend
watch.body: National Assembly vote on the revenue side of the 2027 budget; deficit target 5% of output from 5.4%. A second protest is called for this weekend.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Brent $110.64, +1.0% (~4am ET); WTI $99.47. Monday's waiver dip is gone: Iran says mines hit two tankers south of Hormuz, Qatar calls talks "increasingly difficult".
10y 5.11%, -2bp overnight (~3:45am ET) after +6bp Monday; 2y 4.76%, flat. October hold 83%, December hike 89%; Fed in blackout to the Oct 28 FOMC.
France 10y 4.92%, -2bp; spread to Bunds 144bp from a 147bp Monday close, widest since 2012. Curfews held overnight. Euro $1.123; DXY 101.76, -0.2% (~3am ET).
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13: no new extremes. Wheat specs at the 86th percentile remain the one fresh read. 5y Treasury longs at the 98th, sixth week, are background.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: SOX up Monday, first gain in 9 sessions. It did not travel: Kospi -3.7%, Nikkei -1.3%, Taiex -1.1% Tuesday; Korea's two memory names -3% to -4%.
Futures (~4am ET): S&P flat, Nasdaq 100 -0.3%, Dow +0.2%; semis ETF -1% pre-market. A Korean AI data-center IPO closed -30% on debut, below issue.
Europe (~4am ET): Stoxx 600 -0.6%, DAX -0.9% after Monday's -0.8%. Hang Seng -1.3% as a 4.5% Q3 GDP beat cut stimulus odds; Jakarta +5.7% after -15% in two sessions.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13, unchanged: Russell 2000 specs 99th percentile, third week; Nasdaq 100 97th, fourth week; VIX shorts 6th. Long index futures against short vol into a -3.7% Kospi day.

single_name.note: Sprinklr: insider-buy rule fired, filing dated Oct 15, new to the list today. Above its 200-day; days to cover 3.5. Long setup, score 5 of 5.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: AI-chain 5y CDS at records: two mega-cap AI names above 100bp, the largest neocloud above 1,000bp. Monday's equity rally did not travel to AI credit.
Hedging has moved from puts to CDS: equity and multi-asset funds are buying protection on AI names. Index CDS volumes this year already exceed all of 2025.
Refunding Nov 4: $3bn cuts to each 20y and 30y auction are expected, issuance shifting to bills. That supply meets an 8-week bill bid that set a record low last week.
sections.positioning: Dealers' HY inventory at the 28th percentile of 3 years, unchanged. Dealer paper is not the overhang; protection buying is.
